observations: Two red gas cylinders stand side by side on pavement in photo 0 and photo 1.
Photo 2 shows a close-up of one red gas cylinder.
The left cylinder in photo 0 displays a white CALOR logo and text including Propane and a phone number.
Photo 2 shows CALOR branding, a diamond hazard symbol, and embossed capacity text near the top that is partly obscured by a watermark.
Both cylinders show surface rust, scratches, and faded paint.
No regulator, hose, or valve operation is shown in any photo.
Photos 0 and 1 show two cylinders, while the seller states only one is for sale.

claims.evidence: Capacity marking in photo 2 is partly obscured; 50kg is not clearly legible.
Photos 0 and 1 show two cylinders together.

risks.risk: Cylinder may be empty or contain an unknown amount of gas.
risks.proof: Video of gas release or a weighbridge receipt showing full weight.

risks.risk: Valve may be damaged, seized, or leaking.
risks.proof: Close-up video of the valve being opened and closed, plus a soapy-water leak test.

risks.risk: Cylinder may have hidden corrosion, cracks, or an expired test date.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the base, seams, and collar, or a valid hydrostatic test certificate.

risks.risk: Actual capacity may be smaller than 50kg.
risks.proof: Clear, unobstructed photo of the embossed capacity marking.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the capacity/weight marking on the cylinder collar or body
Video showing the valve being opened and closed
Photo of the cylinder on a weighing scale
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a used Calor gas cylinder; despite unverified capacity and hidden condition risks, it can be priced at worst case (empty, non-working valve, unproven size).
